newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-DLJ optimistic on M&A, new issues.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-DLJ optimistic on M&A, new issues.

text.p: Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Inc Chairman and Chief Executive John Chalsty said he is optimistic about the firm's 1997 prospects, citing mergers and underwriting as strong points.

"We're not in fear and trembling of 1997," Chalsty said during a telephone interview. "We're going into this year with a fair amount of optimism. We have a significant backlog and more importantly significant momentum."
He declined to comment directly on DLJ's earnings per share prospects for the coming year.
Earlier today, DLJ reported fourth quarter earnings of $1.15 per share, up from $0.93 a year ago. For the year, the firm earned a record $291.3 million or $4.55 per share.
During the quarter, DLJ benefitted from sharply higher fee revenues, a function of the firm's efforts to build its merger business, Chalsty said.
"Fees were very strong and we were quite pleased about that because they reflect great growth in our merger and acquisitions practice," he said.
Fee revenues jumped nearly 53 percent to $160.7 million in the quarter from $105.1 million a year ago, while underwriting surged 56 percent to $193.7 million from $124.0 million.
"I think our underwriting income probably surprised people," Chalsty said. "We maintained our very strong number four ranking and actually increased our market share."

According to information provided by Securities Data Co, DLJ served as lead manager on some $8.0 billion in equity deals in 1996, good for fourth behind Goldman Sachs & Co's, $16.6 billion, Merrill Lynch and Co Inc's $14.2 billion and Morgan Stanley Group Inc's $12.6 billion.
In percentage terms, DLJ won a 7.0 percent market share, up from 6.2 percent in 1995, but still well behind Morgan Stanley's 11.0 percent third place slice.
Chalsty has few illusions about cracking the top three in the near future but he is hoping to narrow the gap.

"We're never modest about our goals," he said, adding, "but all three are equally determined to keep their position and are terrific firms with big shares. As long as we can keep our position and grow our market share, we'll be pleased."

Chalsty noted the firm increased its edge in the high-yield bond underwriting arena, stretching its industry leading share to about 20 percent in 1996 from 16 percent in 1995, and has a record backlog for this time of year.
"We're very optimistic about the high yield business," he said. "We have a very big backlog and the business doesn't seem to us to be tailing off at all."

Clearly, the outlook for equity underwriting will hinge on the health of the market in 1997. Chalsty said the firm continues to have "a constructive view" on the market but said DLJ had alternatives available were the market to disappoint.

"We just closed a $3 billion fund investment fund here recently and have other equity funds as well," he said. "If you put all our equity funds together, you could argue we have $7 billion of firepower" available were the market to dip.
Shares in DLJ rose 5/8 to 37-1/4 as of mid-afternoon.
